facts.value: decideFighter writes the requested facing direction and uses Fighter.kind to select an entry branch. Ness, Peach and Mr. Game & Watch receive the fighter object through specialized entry functions, without the supplied stick_angle argument. Pikachu and Pichu receive common doEnter(gobj, stick_angle) followed by Fighter_SetEffectHitlagCallbacks; all remaining kinds receive common doEnter(gobj, stick_angle) without that additional setup.
facts.rationale: Corrects the claim that every selected branch consumes the previously derived angle. The canonical branch arguments distinguish specialized entry from common angle selection.

evidence.why: Facing assignment and complete branch-specific argument flow.

facts.value: Supports grounded forward-smash execution through signed horizontal direction values and standard motion-entry constants. The general input paths derive a left/right sign from stick X, while the Dash main-stick path preserves current facing. The sign becomes fighter-relative only when multiplied by current facing to choose a forward or backward item throw; fighter and applicable item-use entries instead assign it to facing_dir. Common straight or angled AttackS4 entry uses frame 0, rate 1 and blend 0.
facts.rationale: Corrects the description of the direction itself as fighter-relative and preserves the Dash exception.

evidence.why: Direction derivation, relative throw comparison and facing writes.

facts.value: Provides the translation unit's compiler-emitted floating-point literal pool used for forward-smash input direction and common motion-state initialization.
facts.rationale: Preserves the supported purpose while removing an unqualified read-only assertion. Restored section-evidence.json, SHA-256 b04845828f39af9b304744fe71c637f63581471cf4b1b5bc547f16071fa45d92, identifies zero, one and minus-one float words but reports different source/split object flags; final runtime protection is not established.

evidence.why: Source-level direction literal use corresponding to the compiled evidence identified in the rationale.
Motion initialization literal use; no permission inference from C.

facts.value: When allow_interrupt is set, initial first-success priority is side special, up special through ftCo_Attack100_CheckInput, neutral special through ftCo_800D6824, down special through ftCo_800D68C0, then grab. If none succeeds, ftCo_800CECE8 is tested independently of allow_interrupt; that helper requires nonzero command variable 0 and an A press for the second-smash entry. If interruption is allowed and no earlier check succeeds, priority continues through forward, up and down smash; forward, up and down tilt; neutral attack; ftCo_80091A4C; ftCo_800DE9D8; jump; dash; ftCo_800D5FB0; turn; and walk. The first successful check ends processing.
facts.rationale: The misleading Attack100 canonical name does not describe rapid-jab behavior here: its implementation dispatches SpecialHi, and the adjacent helpers dispatch SpecialN and SpecialLw. Preserves both interrupt gates, command gating and early-return reachability.

evidence.why: Exact call order, interrupt gates and early returns.
Independent proof of neutral, down and up special dispatch.
Second-smash command window and entry behavior.
